newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUISENBERG PLAYS DOWN "NUMBER FETISHISM" OVER EMU.
newsitem.headline: DUISENBERG PLAYS DOWN "NUMBER FETISHISM" OVER EMU.

text.p: Wim Duisenberg, outgoing Dutch central bank president and president elect of the European Monetary Institute, warned against "fetishism" in interpreting economic and monetary union admission criteria.
In an interview with leading Dutch financial daily Het Financieele Dagblad published on Friday, Duisenberg said admission criteria should not be interpreted in too "bookkeeperly" a manner.
The 15 nations of the European Union have agreed to a raft of measures aimed at providing stability as the bloc moves towards economic and monetary union in 1999.
"I want to keep away from that sort of fetishism about figures," Duisenberg told the newspaper, echoing similar remarks he made earlier this month.
"The criteria have done a fantastic job in recent years. They have contributed to (helping) countries like Italy, Spain, Portugal and France move towards achieving the criteria," he said.

Duisenberg, however, denied he was relaxing the three percent benchmark maximum budget deficit which is one lynchpin of EMU. "I stick to the three percent but in the (Maastricht) treaty it doesn't say three percent," he said.
"What is the sanctity of three percent? It happens to be an average figure for Europe whan the Maastricht Treaty was drawn up," he told the newspaper.
